title: Raised By Wolves Brings Blade Runner's AI Fascination And Dune's Religious Fanaticism To A Remote Alien World
text: Raised By Wolves Brings Blade Runner's AI Fascination And Dune's Religious Fanaticism To A Remote Alien World HBO's Raised by Wolves, executive produced by Ridley Scott, merges the artificial intelligence exploration of Blade Runner with the religious conflict theme of Dune. Set on the alien planet Kepler-22b, the series follows two androids raising human children after a devastating Earth war, examining the boundaries between artificial consciousness, faith, and family. Despite its rich thematic depth, the show was cancelled by HBO Max in 2022. When it comes to hard sci-fi, two franchises with almost impossible thematic depth to match are Blade Runner and Dune. Both properties treat their sci-fi concepts like advanced artificial intelligence and engineered societies with dangerous concentrations of absolute power as much more than futuristic window dressing. Both Dune and Blade Runner use spectacular technology to explore uncomfortable truths about how technological innovation can quickly lead to irreversible change, with progress almost always coming with a huge cost. Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover However, despite having similar levels of intellectual ambition, Blade Runner and Dune are worlds apart. One explores manufactured life through the lens of a rain-soaked neon-lit cyberpunk dystopia.The other examines ideas like religion, empire, and ecological exploitation across a sprawling interstellar civilization. Their philosophical concerns overlap, but their stories, settings and atmospheres are totally different. That distinction makes HBO's Raised by Wolves, which counts Blade Runner's Ridley Scott among its executive producers, essential viewing for fans of either franchise.Raised By Wolves Plot OverviewAiring for two seasons between 2020 and 2022, Raised by Wolves is a thematically complex tale of two androids raising children on the uninhabited planet Kepler-22b after religious warfare devastates Earth. It combines Blade Runner's anxieties about artificial life with Dune's fascination with religious doctrine and control, while also developing an unsettling identity entirely its own.It's a series stacked to the brim with strange mysteries set in an unforgiving alien landscape, all underpinned by an exploration of where the boundary between artificial intelligence and genuine personhood truly is and how ideas like faith and family blur the lines. Raised By Wolves Brings Blade Runner's AI Fascination To Dune's Religious Fanaticism Raised by Wolves has plenty of tangible creative connections to Blade Runner and Dune.Blade Runner director Ridley Scott was an executive producer of the show, and also directed its first two episodes. The show's creator, Aaron Guzikowski, has also collaborated with Dune trilogy director Denis Villeneuve in the past.Androids And Emotional AttachmentHowever, the series' similarities to both go beyond its creative team. It's a spiritual successor to both franchises in many ways, especially when it comes to its core themes. The thematic connection between Raised by Wolves and Blade Runner is through the androids Mother (Amanda Collin) and Father (Abubakar Salim). Tasked with raising human children as atheists, these synthetic caregivers find themselves developing genuine emotional attachments that complicate the distinction between programming and genuine feeling.Father's insecurity and Mother's fierce protectiveness are used to examine whether artificial consciousness could develop true familial bonds just like human beings. Just like in Ridley Scott's Blade Runner, supposedly simulated emotions soon start to feel more convincing than the humanity displayed by actual people.Meanwhile, the Dune parallels emerge through the religious group known as the Mithraic, whose worship of Sol is used as a justification for violence. Prophecy shapes how survivors of the holy war on Earth interpret the mysteries of Kepler-22b, turning unexplained events into apparent confirmation of their beliefs. Just like the Dune movies and books, Raised by Wolves is fascinated by the ease with which religious authority can be used to manipulate well-meaning people into committing truly atrocious acts.Religious Fanaticism In KeplerWhere the true genius of Raised by Wolves lies is that its artificial intelligence and religious fanaticism storylines are inseparable. Questions around who should raise humanity and the purpose of faith and belief following catastrophe are parts of the same conversations. It may explore the same philosophical territories as both Dune and Blade Runner, but Raised by Wolves investigates these themes in a way that's entirely its own.The Fate Of Raised By Wolves Is Truly Tragic Few streaming-era sci-fi shows have committed so completely to a complex philosophical exploration quite like Raised by Wolves. The series dived head-first into ideas like domestic tension, religious warfare, and the challenges of settling on an alien world. This meant it was intellectually demanding, but also incredibly satisfying.HBO Max Cancellation DecisionThere are few, if any, sci-fi series out there like it, and this ambition makes its eventual cancellation an especially difficult pill to swallow. HBO Max ended Raised by Wolves in 2022 after two seasons, leaving the story unfinished and the second season's cliffhanger ending unresolved. The decision followed the WarnerMedia-Discovery merger, with Raised by Wolves being one of several HBO shows that didn't survive the corporate shift.

Both properties treat their sci-fi concepts like advanced artificial intelligence and engineered societies with dangerous concentrations of absolute power as much more than futuristic window dressing. One explores manufactured life through the lens of a rain-soaked neon-lit cyberpunk dystopia.The other examines ideas like religion, empire, and ecological exploitation across a sprawling interstellar civilization.
